THE FINAL GAME of the regular schedule for 1938 takes place today. The Giants
of 1938 have lived up to the early season promise which caused us to predict a team
Your support has been wholehearted, and we take this means of conveying to
you the gratitude of the New York Giants management and playing personnel. With-
out your support in the stands the team could not have carried on to its present
It will be the earnest endeavor of Coach Steve Owen and his players today to
show their appreciation of that support by exerting every effort to win the eastern
title and quality for the National League playoff against the western champion.
This marks the close of the fourteenth season for the Giants in the Polo Grounds
and we trust that you will be back for the start of the fifteenth next fall. It is our
aim to constantly strive for better football and better Giant teams to represent you
We would like to call your attention to the 1938 Giants team picture printed on
the last page of today's program and also to the ballot on the opposite page. If you
have a favorite Giant player or perhaps your favorite is one of the visiting players
you've seen this fall send in your vote and help him win a place on the all-star pro
team which will play the champions next month in Los Angeles.
The first annual competition for the Leonard Grant Memorial will come to
a conclusion today between the halves. Five schoolboy punters representing
the best kickers from all sections of the metropolitan area will meet in the final
to decide the best kicker in this section. Each finalist has qualified for the final
in previous district competitions and each has won his district competition with
The order in which the competitors will kick is to be decided by lot and will

There are differences in rules for games
played in the National Football League and
under intercollegiate rules. We would like to
call your attention to these major differences:
1. The goal posts are on the goal line (not
2. Forward passes are permitted from any

3. The penalty for a forward pass thrown
beyond the line of scrimmage is loss of down
and five yards from the spot such pass is made.
4. A forward pass on fourth down is not a
touchback if it goes over the goal line providing
the pass originated outside the 20-yard line.
In other words if the pass was thrown from
the 25-yard line on fourth down it reverts to
the defending team at that point.
5. On a kickoff the receiving team is not
